slides.title: Two-dimensional layout
slides.main: Grid lays out along two axes at once: display: grid makes children grid items.

captions: Flexbox runs along one axis, grid along two at once: rows and columns
The container needs only display: grid, and its direct children become grid items
Lines are numbered from one; between neighbors is a track, at a row-column crossing a cell

slides.title: Columns and rows
slides.main: Track sizes are separated by spaces; fr divides the free space left over.

captions: Columns and rows are a list of sizes separated by spaces: pixels, percentages and the special fr unit
Fixed sizes and gaps are subtracted, and the free space is what remains
The remainder is split by shares: 1fr and 2fr make the second column twice as wide
Equal tracks are written with repeat: repeat(3, 1fr) is three equal columns

frames.text: fixed tracks: the width doesn't change

slides.title: Gaps and implicit tracks
slides.main: gap is only between tracks; extra items create implicit rows.

captions: gap: one value for all, or two: first between rows, then between columns
gap adds no margins at the edges, only space between neighbors
More items than cells in the explicit grid: the browser adds implicit rows, sized by content
grid-auto-rows sets the size of implicit rows, for example each new one 46px

frames.text: frame around the grid: no gaps at the edges
the grid grows with the data

slides.title: Track limits
slides.main: minmax(min, max) keeps a track within limits; minmax(0, 1fr) prevents blowout.

captions: minmax(min, max): the column grows from the minimum to the maximum when there is room
Container narrower than the minimum: the column stays at the minimum and sticks out
auto, min-content and max-content: by content, the narrowest and the widest
1fr is never smaller than its content: a long word blows up the column; minmax(0, 1fr) keeps columns equal

frames.text: lots of room: the column grows up to 1fr
won't shrink below the minimum: it overflows
1fr: the word blew up the column, shares are unequal
columns are equal, the word can wrap or be cut

slides.title: Responsive grid, no media queries
slides.main: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)): as many columns as fit.

captions: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)): a wide window gets all five columns in one row
The browser counts how many minimum-width columns fit and stretches them to the full width
On a phone one column remains, and not a single media query
auto-fill keeps empty tracks, auto-fit collapses them and stretches the rest

frames.text: auto-fit: empty ones collapse, the rest get wider

slides.title: Placing by lines
slides.main: Lines are numbered from 1, negative ones from the end; span sets the length.

captions: grid-column: 1 / 3: from line one to line three, that is two columns
Instead of an end line, span: 2 / span 2 starts at line two and takes two columns
Negative numbers count from the end: 1 / -1 spans the row, however many columns there are
For rows, grid-row does the same: span 2 makes an item two rows tall

slides.title: Named areas
slides.main: The layout is drawn in words; areas are only rectangles.

captions: grid-template-areas draws the grid in words: each row in quotes, one name per cell
The same name in a row merges into one area: the header takes both columns
An item only has to name its area: grid-area: header
An area must be a rectangle: an L-shaped one is invalid

frames.text: the layout reads like a sketch on paper
two "header"s in a row: one area across two columns
each item names its own area
L-shaped area: the rule is dropped

slides.title: Alignment
slides.main: items: inside cells, content: the grid in the container, self: one item.

captions: justify-items: horizontal inside the cell, align-items: vertical: start, center, end
place-items: center: both alignments at once, the item sits right in the middle of the cell
For one item: align-self and justify-self; only it goes to the corner
If the tracks don't fill the space, justify-content, align-content and place-content move the grid

frames.text: align-self: end + justify-self: end: middle item only
justify-content: start: tracks narrower than the container

slides.title: Auto-placement
slides.main: dense fills the holes, but the order on screen differs from the document order.

captions: Row by row by default: the wide B didn't fit and moved down, leaving a hole in the first row
grid-auto-flow: column: a column is filled top to bottom first
dense is tight packing: C takes the hole, and D follows
On screen the order is A C B D, in the document A B C D: the keyboard follows the document

frames.text: a hole is left in the first row
grid-auto-flow: row dense: the hole is filled
in the document: A → B → C → D
on screen: A → C → B → D

slides.title: Nested grids
slides.sub: A grid in a cell, and subgrid
slides.main: A nested grid has its own tracks; subgrid takes the parent's tracks.

captions: A grid item can itself be a grid, with its own tracks inside its own cell
Each card has its own layout: texts of different length, so the buttons end up at different heights
subgrid: cards take the parent's rows, so titles, texts and buttons sit on shared lines
The card spans three parent rows and takes them: grid-template-rows: subgrid

frames.text: inside a cell, its own 2×2 grid
subgrid: shared rows, buttons on one line
the parent sets the rows, the card takes them

slides.title: Typical layouts
slides.main: Two or three properties: a page, a gallery, cards; no percentages or math.

captions: Page: a fixed-width menu, flexible content, header and footer across both columns
On a narrow screen, inside a media query, the columns turn into one
Gallery and cards are a responsive grid; a tile may take several cells
A page is one grid declaration: no percentages, no math

frames.text: @media: one column, items one under another
gallery and card row: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(…, 1fr))
tracks described, the browser computes the layout

slides.title: Grid and flexbox
slides.main: Flex is a row and content leads; grid is structure and the container leads; together is best.

captions: Flexbox: one axis, item width set by content: menus, buttons, toolbars
Grid: columns and rows shared by all items, sizes set by the container
Grid builds the page frame, flexbox lines up the row inside the header
Pick the approach that reads more easily: often both work

frames.text: flex: width set by content, one axis
grid: columns and rows shared by all
frame is grid, header row is flex

slides.title: Debugging and checklist
slides.main: The grid badge in DevTools draws lines and names; fr, minmax, gap, auto-fit, areas by meaning.

captions: The grid badge next to an element: lines, their numbers and area names drawn over the page
The layout panel turns on line numbers, area names and track sizes
Tracks set with fractions and minmax, gaps with gap
Responsive with auto-fit, areas named by meaning, document order matches the screen
